text:
Alice K: heads-up — seeing a big spike in spot GPU evictions in eu-west1 since 06:10 UTC, a bunch of model-serving pods got evicted and the autoscaler didn't bring up fallback nodes fast enough :grimacing:
Ben I: saw it too, alerts fired. autoscaler logs show failed launches due to quota/insufficient capacity in the fallback nodepool
Carla S: can you paste the autoscaler error?
Alice K: here's a trimmed log from the scaler: ```E0307 06:12:31 cluster_autoscaler.go:123] Failed to scale up: Failed to create instance template: quotaExceeded: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project
Details: attempted add 4 GPUs```
Dmitri R: we're hitting two problems: (1) spot eviction wave in the available instance types, (2) fallback nodepool needs different SKU mix + we don't have reserved quota in eu-west1
Ben I: current setup uses one spot-heavy nodepool and one tiny reserved warm pool (size=1) with taint standby=true:NoSchedule
Carla S: that single warm node is getting eaten when we need >1 failed nodes. Suggest: expand warm pool to 3 with smaller instance types and keep them tainted, then critical model deployments get tolerations. cheaper than failingover to distant region
Alice K: +1. cost math quick note: adding 2 n1-standard* + 1 GPU reserved ~ increases baseline by ~0.6k/mo vs an outage hit (SLO penalties + queuing) of multiple k for a few hours
Dmitri R: also propose autoscaler config tweaks: set expander: "priority" and add mixed-instances policy so fallback launches mix preemptible-friendly SKUs and non-spot SKUs. Also increase scale-up buffer: --scale-up-from-zero true and reduce scale-up-cooldown to 15s for critical pools
Ben I: watch out for API rate limits when we drop cooldown too low. But agree on expander change.
Carla S: we should also add a nodetemplate for 'standby-gpu' with gpu-type=A100-small and taint standby=true:NoSchedule. Deployments use toleration and priorityClass=high for prod-inference
Infra Bot: incident summary generated: evictions=78 in 17m; affected services: model-serve-prod (partial), rerank-svc (briefly degraded). Rolling median latency +85% during event.
Alice K: quick mitigation now: (1) increase warm pool from 1->3, (2) temporarily allow cross-region fallback to us-west2 for non-PII jobs, (3) patch scaler to prefer standby pool for critical nodegroups. I'm starting (1) now.
Ben I: I'm on (2). Will flip routing for batch queues to use remote region.
Dmitri R: I'll open a ticket to request GPU quota bump in eu-west1 and schedule a test to simulate evictions so autoscaler+taint+toleration path is exercised.
Carla S: for postmortem let's capture metrics: eviction_rate, time_to_first_fallback_node, pods_pending_by_priority. Also run a chaos test next cadence to validate warm pool sizing.
Alice K: added a short-term alert: alert if evictions_per_min > 5 AND fallback_nodes_available < 2 -> P1 page.
EvictBot: ran simulated eviction test in staging, results: with warm pool=3 tolerations ok, cold start to 3 nodes ~ 2m10s, pods become Ready ~ 2m50s.
Ben I: sounds reasonable. Long-term we should explore mixed provisioning: reserved baseline + opportunistic spot overlay + predictive pre-warm for known traffic windows.
Dmitri R: agreed. I'll draft a proposal with cost comparisons and rollout plan.
Alice K: thanks team. Will keep thread updated as warm pool scales and metrics come in. :eyes:
